title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M_{1,1} is the moduli stack of elliptic curves over Q. Its geometric fundamental group is the profinite completion SL(2,Z)^. Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) acts on it by outer automorphisms. Composing with the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ) = ∏_p SL(2,Z_p) gives the outer action (4) of Γ_Q on SL(2,Ẑ). This comes from the monodromy on the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve: Γ_Q acts through an element of GL(2,Ẑ) of determinant χ(σ), where χ is the cyclotomic character.

Previous page. Scalars λ ∈ Ẑ^* = centre of GL(2,Ẑ) act trivially by conjugation on SL(2,Ẑ), and det(λ) = λ². Hence the map Ẑ^* ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)/SL(2,Ẑ) → Autext SL(2,Ẑ) factors through Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}; this is (5). Moreover, u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) induces an inner automorphism iff u ∈ SL(2,Ẑ)·Ẑ^*. The reason is that the centraliser of SL(2,Ẑ) in GL(2,Ẑ) is the scalars. So (5) is injective.

This page.
- Consequently the kernel of the outer action (4) equals the kernel of the composite (6): Γ_Q → Ẑ^* → Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}.
- By class field theory over Q (Kronecker–Weber), Ẑ^* = Gal(Q^ab/Q). Its quotient by squares is (Γ_Q^ab)/2, the Galois group of the maximal multiquadratic extension Q(√-1, √2, √p : p prime).
- So the outer action on SL(2,Ẑ) factors through this 'multiquadratic' quotient and is faithful on it.
- The margin adds the finite-level version: the outer action on SL(2,Z/n) factors through (Z/n)^* (via χ mod n), and in fact through (Z/n)^*/squares.

Programme. Regard Γ_Q as a subgroup of Autext SL(2,Z)^. This subgroup must satisfy rather strong conditions:
- (i) it preserves the distinguished normal subgroup ker(SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ)), the congruence kernel (7);
- (ii) the induced outer action on SL(2,Ẑ) comes from a homomorphism Γ → Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}.

Grothendieck then begins to pin this homomorphism down using the 'loop subgroups' (inertia at the cusp ∞ of M_{1,1}). The continuation on the next page:
- the inertia T ≅ Ẑ(1) maps to a unipotent subgroup (1 0; n 1) of SL(2,Ẑ);
- any outer automorphism preserving the conjugacy class of this image acts on T by a unique scalar;
- for Galois elements that scalar is the cyclotomic character.

This is a step towards a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type characterisation of the image of Γ_Q in Out(SL(2,Z)^) by group-theoretic conditions: cusp/inertia preservation together with compatibility with the congruence quotient.
errors: The text 'le noyau de (5)' is inconsistent, since (5) has just been shown injective. Logically it must be the kernel of (4) (equivalently, of the outer action on SL(2,Ẑ)). Likely a misreading or slip; the image appears to show (4).
'Autext Sl(2,Ẑ)^' should be Autext SL(2,Z)^, the profinite completion of the discrete group. This is a notational slip, judging by the context of (7).

Minor: the factorisation claim implicitly uses that the outer action of Γ_Q on SL(2,Ẑ) is the Tate-module one, of determinant χ. This was established on the previous page (composite of (2) and (3)), so there is no gap.

ideas.what: Outer Galois action on SL(2,Ẑ) (congruence quotient of π1(M_{1,1})) factors through χ mod squares, i.e. through Gal of the maximal multiquadratic extension of Q, and is faithful there
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the congruence quotient via the Tate module / cyclotomic character; Out(SL2(Ẑ)) contribution of GL2/scalars
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Shimura, Ihara-era arithmetic of modular curves)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or Longue Marche as stated, to my knowledge; unsure

ideas.what: Characterising the image of Γ_Q in Out(SL(2,Z)^) by group-theoretic conditions: preservation of the congruence kernel and of the cusp inertia class, with induced action via a character
ideas.modern_name: Genus-one (M_{1,1}) analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group; Galois action on π1(M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997); Nakamura; Hain–Matsumoto (elliptic/M_{1,1} Galois action)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme sketches the 'tour de Teichmüller' and the role of M_{1,1}; the specific congruence-kernel condition is not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Cusp inertia ('sous-groupes-lacets') maps to unipotent subgroups; outer automorphisms preserving their class act on inertia by a scalar, equal to χ for Galois elements
ideas.modern_name: Inertia/cusp preservation condition; cyclotomic character via the inertia action (Ihara)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; standard in anabelian / GT literature
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (lacets)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes defining a subgroup of Out(SL(2,Z)^) by requiring invariance of the congruence kernel ker(SL(2,Z)^→SL(2,Ẑ)) plus induced action through Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}, as a candidate genus-one constraint on the Galois image. Using the congruence kernel as a structural invariant in a GT-type definition is not, to my knowledge, a standard axiom in the GT literature, which uses braid/pentagon/inertia relations.
missed.quote: ce sous-groupe Γ est astreint à des conditions assez fortes : invarier le sous-groupe distingué noyau de (7) Sl(2,Z)^ → Sl(2,Ẑ) et induire sur Sl(2,Ẑ) une opération extérieure provenant d'un hom Γ → Ẑ*/Ẑ*²
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether the congruence kernel is characteristic in SL(2,Z)^ and how such conditions cut down Out(SL(2,Z)^) relates to current work on Galois action on π1(M_{1,1}) and on profinite GT variants. It is a modest but explicit, untested axiom.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation (outer Galois action on SL(2,Ẑ) factors faithfully through the multiquadratic quotient) is elementary and folklore. The programme of characterising Γ_Q in Out(SL(2,Z)^) anticipates genus-one GT ideas known from later literature. The congruence-kernel invariance condition is a minor unexplored detail.
transcription_corrections: The '300' above the first line is Grothendieck's own page number (of the 293–650 numbering), not part of the mathematics.
'le noyau de (5)' should most likely read 'le noyau de (4)'.
Margin NB plausibly reads: 'NB l'op. ext. de Γ_Q sur Sl(2,Z/nZ) se factorise par ((Z/nZ)^*)/((Z/nZ)^*)^2, i.e. via χ'.
'[-operant-]' is a struck word after Γ_Q, possibly 'opérant'.
'[-propres-] invariance' is better read as '[struck] invarier'.
